cards.text: Alright, friend, this love song comes from the sons of Korah, a family of Levites who praised the LORD (2 Chronicles 20:19). It's written for the choirmaster, to the tune of “The Lilies.” The writer says his heart is stirred by a noble theme, and his tongue is the pen of a skillful writer.

cards.question: The writer's heart is stirred by a noble theme. Who does he say he's reciting his verses to?

cards.text: He opens BIG, telling the king, “You are the most handsome of men; grace has anointed your lips…” Nobody has EVER opened a poem to me like that, friend!

cards.question: The writer tells the king that God has blessed him forever.

cards.text: Then the song shifts gears. The writer tells the king to strap his sword at his side and appear in his majesty and splendor.

cards.question: With the king's sword strapped at his side, the writer calls him a mighty ___.

cards.text: The writer tells the king to ride forth in his splendor, in victory, on behalf of truth and humility and justice. His arrows pierce the hearts of the king's foes.

cards.question: With the king's arrows flying, the nations rise up and drive him back.

cards.text: Then the writer says, “Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever…”, and Hebrews says that line is about the Son, Jesus (Hebrews 1:8). The first time I read that, I dropped a WHOLE tray of dough.

cards.question: This throne endures forever and ever. What does the writer say is the scepter of the kingdom?
The psalm says God has anointed the one on this throne above his companions with the oil of joy. Why?

answers.text: He loved righteousness and hated wickedness
He was the strongest of all his companions
He was born the oldest son of a king

cards.text: Now the writer catches a whiff: the king's garments are all fragrant with myrrh and aloes and cassia. Me? I smell like warm dough and a little bit of oven mitt.

cards.question: The harps play from palaces of ivory to make the king ___.

cards.text: Then the writer looks around the room. The daughters of kings are among the king's honored women.

cards.question: Adorned with the gold of Ophir, who stands at the king's right hand?

cards.text: Now the song turns to someone new: “Listen, O daughter!” The writer tells her to consider and incline her ear, and to forget her people and her father's house.

cards.question: The daughter is told to forget her people and her father's house. What does the writer say the king will do?

cards.text: Then the writer tells her, “bow to him, for he is your lord.”
Then the writer says the Daughter of Tyre will come with a gift, and Tyre is a city by the sea. When I got stuck in the back of a junk drawer, nobody brought me ANYTHING!

cards.question: The writer tells the daughter he's been speaking to that men of wealth will seek her ___.

cards.text: Now the princess is all glorious in her chamber, her gown embroidered with gold. My apron's embroidered too, friend, with FLOUR.

cards.question: Dressed in colorful garments, the princess is led to the ___.
The princess's virgin companions are brought in too. They're led into the palace of the king with fear and trembling.

cards.text: Then the song looks way down the road to the next generation. Sons will succeed the fathers who came before them.

cards.question: The writer tells the king he will make his sons princes throughout the land.

cards.text: And the writer signs off with a promise: he'll commemorate this name through all generations. ALL of them, friend, and I can't even promise a batch won't burn.

cards.question: The writer will commemorate this name through all generations. Because of that, what does he say the nations will do forever and ever?
